facts.statement: Dwardius is an extinct genus of sharks belonging to the family Cardabiodontidae.
facts.quote: Dwardius is an extinct genus of cardabiodontid sharks

facts.statement: Dwardius lived during the Cretaceous period in regions that are now Australia, England, France, and India.
facts.quote: which existed during the Cretaceous period in what is now Australia, England, France, and India

facts.statement: The genus Dwardius was described by Mikael Siverson in 1999, elevating the species Cretalamna woodwardi, originally described by J. Hermann in 1977.
facts.quote: It was described by Mikael Siverson in 1999, as a new genus for the species Cretalamna woodwardi, which had been described by J. Hermann in 1977

facts.statement: The species D. siversoni was described by V.I. Zhelezko in 2000 from fossils found in the middle Albian of northeastern France.
facts.quote: Another species, D. siversoni, was described from the middle Albian of northeastern France by V.I. Zhelezko in 2000

facts.statement: The species D. sudindicus was described in 2011 by Underwood, Goswami, Prasad, Verma, and Flynn from the Cretaceous Karai Formation in India.
facts.quote: A new species, D. sudindicus, was described by Charlie J. Underwood, Anjali Goswami, G.V.R. Prasad, Omkar Verma, and John J. Flynn in 2011, from the Cretaceous Karai Formation of India

facts.statement: Dwardius is classified within the parent group Cardabiodontidae.
Dwardius belongs to the class Chondrichthyes.
Dwardius lived from the Aptian to the Santonian stages, between 121.4 and 83.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Santonian (121.4 to 83.6 million years ago)
